title: Entropion & Cicatrizing Conjunctivitis: A Clinical Deep Dive
summary: A comprehensive guide to the diagnosis, pathophysiology, and multi-modal management of eyelid malpositions and the complex landscape of cicatrizing conjunctival diseases. Essential for residents managing trichiasis, dermatochalasis, and cicatricial entropion.

sections.title: Clinical Definitions
sections.content: Entropion is the inversion of the eyelid margin towards the globe. This results in the eyelashes and outer skin rubbing against the ocular surface, leading to mechanical irritation, trichiasis, and potential corneal scarring or ulceration. Unlike ectropion, it is frequently symptomatic from the onset.

sections.title: Pathophysiology: The Involutional Triad
content: Horizontal Eyelid Laxity: Stretching of the medial/lateral canthal tendons.
Vertical Instability: Disinsertion or attenuation of the lower lid retractors (capsulopalpebral fascia).
Orbicularis Override: Preseptal orbicularis moves superiorly over the pretarsal orbicularis during blinking.
Tarsal Plate Atrophy: Loss of structural rigidity in the tarsus.

sections.title: Foster Staging of OCP
content: Stage I: Chronic conjunctivitis and subepithelial fibrosis.
Stage II: Fornix shortening (especially inferior).
Stage III: Symblepharon formation.
Stage IV: Ankyloblepharon and surface keratinization.

sections.title: Clinical Examination Checklist
content: Snap-back Test: Assess horizontal laxity.
Distraction Test: Lid pulled >10mm from globe indicates laxity.
Excursion of Lower Lid: Check for retractor disinsertion (decreased movement on downgaze).
Slit Lamp: Look for Arlt's line (superior tarsal scarring) and trichiasis.
Fluorescein Staining: Check for PEEs or corneal ulcers.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Ocular Emergencies
content: Corneal Opacification or Perforation due to persistent lash abrasion.
Rapidly progressive Symblepharon indicating active OCP/Autoimmune flare.
Lid Margin Keratinization causing irreversible corneal surface damage.
Microbial Keratitis secondary to epithelial defects.

rows: Transverse lid blepharotomy with marginal rotation
Shortening of the lid at the lateral canthus

sections.title: Managing Cicatricial Entropion (Upper Lid)
content: 1. Address underlying inflammation (e.g., Dapsone/Cyclophosphamide for OCP).
2. Tarsal Grooving (Streatfeild-Snellen): Wedge excision of tarsus.
3. Posterior Lamella Grafting: Mucous membrane (buccal), hard palate, or amniotic membrane.
4. Terminal Tarsal Rotation (Ballen): For severe upper lid cases.

sections.title: Landmark Study: The SAFE Strategy
content: S: Surgery for Trichiasis.
A: Antibiotics (Azithromycin) for active infection.
F: Facial cleanliness.
E: Environmental improvement (water/sanitation).
WHO target: Global elimination of trachoma as a public health problem.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Resident
content: Differentiate Trichiasis (misdirected lashes) from Distichiasis (extra row from Meibomian glands).
Always check for a 'hidden' upper lid entropion in cases of unexplained corneal staining.
In OCP, never perform surgery during an active inflammatory flare if possible.
Dermatochalasis can coexist but usually masks the severity of the entropion.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup for Scarring
content: Conjunctival Biopsy: Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF) to look for linear basement membrane zone deposits.
Microbiology: Swabs for Chlamydia PCR or bacterial cultures.
Systemic Screen: HLA-B12 (SJS), skin biopsy for Pemphigoid.
Schirmer's Test: Assess associated aqueous tear deficiency.

sections.title: Prognosis & Complications
sections.content: Surgical success for involutional entropion is high (>90% with combined horizontal/vertical tightening). Cicatricial cases have a guarded prognosis and often require multiple interventions. Complications include recurrence, overcorrection (ectropion), and lid margin notch formation.
